text: After two cancelled trips we finally did Bokta Peak Climbing in May. Worth the wait. The climb to 6150 m was the hardest thing we've done, but the view from the top made it worthwhile. Bikash had a good sense of humour, which helped on the long days. Hot showers cost a few hundred rupees and were worth every one of them. A few of the meals were lukewarm, which was a shame because the rest of the food was good. No regrets at all.

title: Lumbini Tour
author: Alessia Ramos
heading: Good, with a couple of gripes
text: The Lumbini Tour was included in our package and we were pleasantly surprised by the standard. The village homestay was the highlight; we learned to make momos with the family. Our driver was punctual and somehow found parking everywhere. The tour ended with a visit to a workshop we would never have found alone. One guide was excellent and the other clearly less experienced, which made the pace uneven.

title: Lumbini Tour
author: Anya Larsen
heading: A week I will not forget
text: A former colleague now lives in Patan and told us to do Lumbini Tour properly. my guide answered questions about daily life, not just the monuments, which I appreciated. Still thinking about that sunrise.

title: Lumbini Tour
author: Sofia Castro
heading: Kids loved it
text: Our daughter was studying the Malla period and Lumbini Tour made her textbook come alive. The mix of Hindu and Buddhist sites in one day was fascinating. Suresh grew up nearby and knew people in every square we walked through. Two weeks on and I am still looking at the photos.

title: Lumbini Tour
author: Marco Bhujel
heading: Brilliant from start to finish
text: We had a long layover and used it on Lumbini Tour instead of sitting in the airport. The old squares and temples were stunning, and the guide explained the history without drowning us in dates. The tea at one lodge on day 2 was basically warm water, and we laughed about it. Would go back with the same team in a heartbeat.

title: Lumbini Tour
author: Hannah Tamang
heading: Exactly what we hoped for
text: I had low expectations for a guided city tour, but Lumbini Tour was genuinely interesting. The wood carvings in the courtyards were the part I keep thinking about. Tickets and entry fees were included, so I never had to queue with cash. No regrets at all.

title: Lumbini Tour
author: Noah Jones
heading: Would still recommend it
text: Booked Lumbini Tour at the last minute in March and it still felt properly organised. The guide's family stories made the history feel less like a lecture. The guide recommended a restaurant for dinner and it was excellent. Pickup and drop-off at the hotel were included. Communication before the trip was slow, with emails sometimes going unanswered for days. Good value for what you get.

title: Lumbini Tour
author: Tomas Brennan
heading: Superb trip
text: The hotel arranged Lumbini Tour for us on our first morning, jet lag and all. The pace was gentle, with plenty of stopping and no herding about. Our guide carried a folder of old photographs, which made the history click. There was plenty of time for photos, not just a quick look and go. Worth the money and the early starts.

title: Lumbini Tour
author: Yuki Grant
heading: Memorable in the best way
text: My husband is not a temple person, and even he enjoyed Lumbini Tour. Traffic in the valley is slow, so the schedule had some slack built in.

title: Lumbini Tour
author: Hugo Fischer
heading: Better than average, a few rough edges
text: Did Lumbini Tour between two treks to give our knees a rest, and learned a lot. The streets were busy and noisy, but that is part of the experience. The guide answered questions patiently, including the silly ones from my group. One activity got swapped at short notice and I only found out that morning. Cannot fault it.

title: Lumbini Tour
author: Toby Magar
heading: So well looked after
text: My sister studies architecture, so Lumbini Tour was her one request for the trip. The local lunch was one of the best meals of the trip. The guide's English was excellent and he had a dry sense of humour. Already trying to work out when we can come back for a longer one.

title: Makalu Base Camp Trek
author: Tara Shrestha
heading: Loved it
text: My partner and I did Makalu Base Camp Trek in April as a break from our desk jobs. The trail was quieter than we expected for April, and we had whole sections to ourselves. Milan had done the route dozens of times and made the tricky sections feel straightforward. Hot showers cost a few hundred rupees and were worth every one of them. Recommended, especially for a first trip to Nepal.

title: Makalu Base Camp Trek
author: Owen Rai
heading: Glad we picked this one
text: Friends who live in Kathmandu told us Makalu Base Camp Trek was the one not to skip. We had one hazy day where the peaks disappeared, which was disappointing, but it cleared by evening. Our duffel bags turned up at the right lodge every single evening. Transfers from Kathmandu were long but comfortable enough, and the flight back was smooth. The flight from Kathmandu was delayed by a few hours, which ate into the first day. Would recommend it to friends without caveats.

title: Makalu Base Camp Trek
author: Jeremiah Peterson
heading: Long days, big views
text: Makalu Base Camp Trek was the main reason for our Nepal trip, and it lived up to the photos I had been staring at for months. The lodge on day 12 had a wood stove going and we stayed up far too late talking. Nabin noticed one of us was struggling and quietly slowed the group down without saying why. The sleeping altitude was well planned, with a rest day exactly when we needed one. One of those trips that stays with you.

title: Makalu Base Camp Trek
author: Isaac Perez
heading: So glad we booked this
text: We were three generations on this trip, ages 19 to 66. Snow on the upper section slowed things down, and the guides adjusted the plan without any fuss. The team in Kathmandu answered emails within a day and sorted permits without us lifting a finger. Still thinking about that sunrise.

title: Makalu Base Camp Trek
author: Freja Rai
heading: Would book again
text: I turned up on my own not knowing a soul and left with five new friends. The last push before the pass took about four hours and felt like eight, but the descent into the next valley was stunning. The kitchen staff produced proper meals at 4,000 m, which is more than I expected. Happy to recommend these guys to anyone heading to Nepal.

title: Makalu Base Camp Trek
author: Rahul Johnson
heading: Would go again
text: My wife had done it before the earthquake and wanted to see what had changed. Trail conditions were good, though the long descent was hard on the knees. Wi-Fi was patchy above the villages, which turned out to be a blessing. No regrets at all.

title: Makalu Base Camp Trek
author: Ana Perkins
heading: Memorable in the best way
text: Four of us from work did Makalu Base Camp Trek in September, none of us with much altitude experience. Teahouses were basic but clean, and the dal bhat kept coming until we could not eat another bite. Would do it again without hesitating.

title: Makalu Base Camp Trek

text: We had two days in Kathmandu before our trek and spent one of them on Nagarkot Sunrise Tour. The drive between sites was long, but the scenery kept it interesting. Good value for what you get.

title: Nagarkot Sunrise Tour
author: Aisha Baxter
heading: Superb trip
text: Did Nagarkot Sunrise Tour solo on my first full day in Nepal and it was a good introduction. I had enough free time at each stop to wander on my own. Bags stayed in the vehicle all day, so I never had to carry anything. Two weeks on and I am still looking at the photos.

title: Nagarkot Sunrise Tour
author: Adam Crawford
heading: Would recommend to anyone
text: Our daughter was studying the Malla period and Nagarkot Sunrise Tour made her textbook come alive. The old town is a maze, and having someone who knows it saved hours. Lunch was included and better than the usual tour buffet.

title: Nagarkot Sunrise Tour
author: Mateo Larsen
heading: Nearly perfect
text: My husband is not a temple person, and even he enjoyed Nagarkot Sunrise Tour. The old squares and temples were stunning, and the guide explained the history without drowning us in dates. The guide recommended a restaurant for dinner and it was excellent. Communication before the trip was slow, with emails sometimes going unanswered for days. Already trying to work out when we can come back for a longer one.

title: Nagarkot Sunrise Tour
author: Jose Jimenez
heading: Proper adventure
text: A former colleague now lives in Patan and told us to do Nagarkot Sunrise Tour properly. Traffic in the valley is slow, so the schedule had some slack built in. I stopped for tea at a place with no other tourists in it. Some of the trail was dusty and busy with mules, more an annoyance than a problem. Cannot fault it.

title: Nagarkot Sunrise Tour
author: Zoey Harrison
heading: Ticked every box
text: We had a day to fill before the flight and Nagarkot Sunrise Tour filled it well. Bhaktapur was my favourite, the wooden carvings and quiet courtyards are unreal. We were given bottled water at every stop. Entry fees were covered, so no fumbling for cash at each gate. Easily the highlight of our holiday.

title: Nagarkot Sunrise Tour
author: Camille Mehta
heading: Very good, not perfect
text: The hotel arranged Nagarkot Sunrise Tour for us on our first morning, jet lag and all. The mountain views from the ridge were a nice surprise on a cultural tour. Tickets and entry fees were included, so we never had to queue with cash. Our group was too big for one guide to manage comfortably. Worth the money and the early starts.

title: Nagarkot Sunrise Tour
author: Linn Bailey
heading: Could not fault the guides
text: Our group of five did Nagarkot Sunrise Tour in April and everyone found something to like. We saw the main sights without ever feeling rushed. The driver found shade to park in every time, small thing but it mattered. The group was a bit large on the first day, though it thinned out after the first village. Happy to recommend these guys to anyone heading to Nepal.

title: Nagarkot Sunrise Tour
author: Marcus Jimenez
heading: One of the best things we did
text: Booked Nagarkot Sunrise Tour because it started late, so no alarm clock was involved. There was a festival rehearsal going on at one square, which nobody had planned for. Wish we had one more rest day built in, the last two days felt long. A solid, well-run trip from start to finish.

title: Nagarkot Sunrise Tour
author: Beatriz Bryant
heading: Absolutely worth it
text: Booked Nagarkot Sunrise Tour at the last minute in September and it still felt properly organised. The streets were busy and noisy, but that is part of the experience. Pickup and drop-off at the hotel were included. The guide gave us a short reading list afterwards, which was a nice touch. The flight from Kathmandu was delayed by a few hours, which ate into the first day. Would do it again without hesitating.

title: Namche to Kathmandu Helicopter Flight – 2 Hours
author: Daniel Novak
heading: Superb trip
text: I booked the Namche to Kathmandu Helicopter Flight – 2 Hours as a surprise for my partner and somehow kept it quiet. Landing at 3450 m for breakfast was surreal, cold and completely quiet. Check-in was quick and someone stayed with us until we boarded. Would recommend it to friends without caveats.

title: Namche to Kathmandu Helicopter Flight – 2 Hours
author: Isla Andersen
heading: Better than average, a few rough edges
text: We took the Namche to Kathmandu Helicopter Flight – 2 Hours on a clear October morning with two friends who had never been to Nepal. The noise-cancelling headsets were a small but welcome touch. Oxygen was on board and the crew showed us how to use it. Hotel pickup was on time, which after a week in Nepal felt like a small miracle. Some of the timings were optimistic, so we ended up walking in the dark on day 2. Cannot fault it.

title: Namche to Kathmandu Helicopter Flight – 2 Hours
author: Callum Ivanov
heading: Best day of the holiday
text: We had one free morning at the end of a work trip and spent it on the Namche to Kathmandu Helicopter Flight – 2 Hours. We got a clear morning, which apparently is not guaranteed, and the peaks were out in full. The crew were calm and friendly and answered all my daft questions. A very good few days.

title: Namche to Kathmandu Helicopter Flight – 2 Hours
author: Lucas Sinclair
heading: Proper adventure
text: The Namche to Kathmandu Helicopter Flight – 2 Hours capped off a week in the mountains, and nothing on the trail compared with it. Equipment looked well maintained and the safety briefing was thorough without being tedious. Our guide for the ground portion was friendly and full of local detail. Easily the highlight of our holiday.

title: Namche to Kathmandu Helicopter Flight – 2 Hours
author: Elif Rai
heading: Great guides, great trip
text: Did the Namche to Kathmandu Helicopter Flight – 2 Hours on my own after my trek finished, mostly for the photos. At one point I was above the clouds with nothing but summits showing. They supplied warm jackets and oxygen, which I did not need but was reassuring. Two weeks on and I am still looking at the photos.

title: Namche to Kathmandu Helicopter Flight – 2 Hours
author: Sarah Lama
heading: Exceeded expectations
text: Took the Namche to Kathmandu Helicopter Flight – 2 Hours in October with a group of six who had all booked separately. Takeoff felt oddly relaxed, more like a scenic drive than an adventure sport. Our pilot Purna has been flying these routes for years and it showed. The whole trip was over by mid-morning, leaving the rest of the day free.

title: Namche to Kathmandu Helicopter Flight – 2 Hours
author: Camille Bianchi
heading: Strong trip, a few letdowns
text: My daughter and I did the Namche to Kathmandu Helicopter Flight – 2 Hours together and neither of us stopped grinning. I expected it to be over too quickly, but the timing felt right. The pilot gave a running commentary on the peaks without talking over the whole flight. Communication before the trip was slow, with emails sometimes going unanswered for days. Would do it again without hesitating.

title: Namche to Kathmandu Helicopter Flight – 2 Hours
author: Luca Mason
heading: A week I will not forget
text: Two of us flew in the morning and went straight back to the hotel for a nap. The pilot pointed out the big peaks by name and banked gently so both sides could see. Nabin made sure everyone got a turn by the window. Worth the money and the early starts.

title: Namche to Kathmandu Helicopter Flight – 2 Hours
author: Charles Stevens
heading: Best money we spent in Nepal
text: Booked the Namche to Kathmandu Helicopter Flight – 2 Hours for a work team morning out, which was a better idea than it sounds. There was a wait for the weather to clear, and nobody pushed us to fly until it was right. The safety briefing was clear and the crew checked straps on every passenger. Breakfast at the landing site was simple but welcome at that altitude.

title: Namche to Kathmandu Helicopter Flight – 2 Hours
author: Alessandro Lee
heading: Better than expected
text: Booked the Namche to Kathmandu Helicopter Flight – 2 Hours for our last morning in Nepal and it turned out to be the best send-off. The peaks looked close enough to touch, which is a strange thing to say from a plane. We got a printed map of the peaks afterwards, which was a nice touch. Good value for what you get.

title: Namche to Kathmandu Helicopter Flight – 2 Hours
author: Sofia Herrera
heading: Smooth from start to finish
text: I am a nervous flyer and nearly cancelled the Namche to Kathmandu Helicopter Flight – 2 Hours. Glad I did not. Both sides of the aircraft get a good run at the mountains, so seating hardly matters. A solid, well-run trip from start to finish.

title: Namche to Kathmandu Helicopter Flight – 2 Hours
author: Kaylee Ramos
heading: Loved every day of it
text: We were unsure whether the Namche to Kathmandu Helicopter Flight – 2 Hours was worth the money. It was. Clouds sat below us for most of the flight, with the peaks sticking out above them. Sunglasses matter more than you would think up there, take the spare pair. Photos from the flight are on my wall now. One of those trips that stays with you.

title: Namche to Kathmandu Helicopter Flight – 2 Hours
author: Victor Kaur
heading: Would do it all again
text: The Namche to Kathmandu Helicopter Flight – 2 Hours had been on my list since a colleague showed me his photos. The whole thing ran to the minute, which after a week in Nepal felt like a small miracle. If you are on the fence, just book it.

title: Namche to Kathmandu Helicopter Flight – 2 Hours
author: Anna James
heading: A trip we will talk about for years
text: Someone at our hotel mentioned the Namche to Kathmandu Helicopter Flight – 2 Hours and we booked it that evening. The landing was soft and the ground crew had us organised within minutes. The hour on the ground was long enough for a proper look around. Still thinking about that sunrise.

title: Nar Phu Valley Trek

text: I turned up on my own not knowing a soul and left with five new friends. Days were long, usually six to eight hours of walking, but the terrain is varied enough that it never dragged. The sirdar kept the group together without ever making the slower ones feel bad. Cannot fault it.

title: Nar Phu Valley Trek

Would recommend it to friends without caveats.

text: I did Pokalde Island and Lobuche Climbing solo in October and joined a small group on the trail. Easily the best thing I did all year. The climb to 6200 m was the hardest thing I've done, but the view from the top made it worthwhile. Nima led me the whole way and quietly fixed every little problem before I noticed it. Recommended, especially for a first trip to Nepal.

title: Pokalde Peak Climbing
author: Elena Sherpa
heading: So much better than expected
text: Booked Pokalde Peak Climbing about ten days out, which is apparently cutting it fine. The view of the range from the last teahouse before the pass on day 9 is burned into my memory. The team in Kathmandu answered emails within a day and sorted permits without us lifting a finger. No regrets at all.

title: Pokalde Peak Climbing
author: Diego Petrov
heading: Very good, not perfect
text: My wife had done it before the earthquake and wanted to see what had changed. Days were long, usually six to eight hours of walking, but the terrain is varied enough that it never dragged. Our duffel bags turned up at the right lodge every single evening. The office helped us store our extra luggage while we were on the trail. The hotel at the start was clean but pretty basic compared to the rest of the trip. Sore legs for three days after, totally worth it.

title: Pokalde Peak Climbing
author: Agnieszka Berry
heading: Would go again
text: A group of us from the climbing gym did Pokalde Peak Climbing in March, and it turned into an annual thing. There were a few steep sections that left us genuinely puffing, but the pace was never rushed. We rented sleeping bags from them and they were clean and warm. The sleeping altitude was well planned, with a rest day exactly when we needed one. Still thinking about that sunrise.

title: Pokalde Peak Climbing
author: Rhea Navarro
heading: Memorable in the best way
text: We had 16 days free in November and Pokalde Peak Climbing looked like the best use of them. The walk out through the villages at the end was a nice way to finish. Hot showers cost a few hundred rupees and were worth every one of them. Transfers from Kathmandu were long but comfortable enough, and the flight back was smooth. Recommended, especially for a first trip to Nepal.

title: Pokalde Peak Climbing
author: Mia Rivera
heading: Hassle free
text: Friends who live in Kathmandu told us Pokalde Peak Climbing was the one not to skip. Crossing the pass was brutal in the wind, but the tea at the teahouse afterwards tasted incredible. Suman had done the route dozens of times and made the tricky sections feel straightforward. Would go back with the same team in a heartbeat.

title: Pokalde Peak Climbing
author: Kiran Bates
heading: Exactly what we hoped for
text: Four of us from work did Pokalde Peak Climbing in March, none of us with much altitude experience. Sleeping at 5800 m was rough on the first night, but the guides kept an eye on everyone. Nabin knew every teahouse owner on the route and got us the better rooms more than once. Already trying to work out when we can come back for a longer one.

title: Pokalde Peak Climbing
author: Maja Reyes
heading: A good trip that could be great
text: My brother and I had Pokalde Peak Climbing on the shortlist for about a year before finally committing, and October turned out to be the right call. The scenery changed every couple of hours, which kept the walking interesting even on the long days. Briefings each evening were clear about the next day's climb and timings. The porters carried more than I would ever want to and still beat us to the lodge. Our group was too big for one guide to manage comfortably. Easily the highlight of our holiday.

title: Pokalde Peak Climbing
author: Nora Nguyen
heading: Loved every day of it

author: Noah Johnson
heading: Everything was easy
text: We were unsure whether the Pokhara Helicopter Sightseeing Tour was worth the money. It was. The peaks looked close enough to touch, which is a strange thing to say from a plane. Cannot fault it.

title: Pokhara Helicopter Sightseeing Tour
author: Linn Baldwin
heading: Really good overall
text: The Pokhara Helicopter Sightseeing Tour had been on my list since a colleague showed me his photos. We got a clear morning, which apparently is not guaranteed, and the peaks were out in full. One guide was excellent and the other clearly less experienced, which made the pace uneven. Still thinking about that sunrise.

title: Pokhara Helicopter Sightseeing Tour
author: Aleksandra Ellis
heading: One of the best things we did
text: Booked the Pokhara Helicopter Sightseeing Tour a week ahead in May and got the seat I wanted. Landing at 3800 m for breakfast was surreal, cold and completely quiet. Nabin warned us which side of the aircraft gets the best light at each stage. Easily the highlight of our holiday.

title: Pokhara Helicopter Sightseeing Tour
author: Eva Sherpa
heading: Smashed our expectations
text: My father flew the Pokhara Helicopter Sightseeing Tour in the nineties and wanted to see it again from the air. Watching the shadows move across the ridges from that height is something else. Dipesh had hot tea waiting for us after the landing, which nobody expected. Booked another trip with them before we even left.

title: Pokhara Helicopter Sightseeing Tour
author: Ruben Kaur
heading: Would book again
text: Booked the Pokhara Helicopter Sightseeing Tour for our last morning in Nepal and it turned out to be the best send-off. The pilot kept checking on the nervous passengers and explained what was happening. The safety briefing was clear and the crew checked straps on every passenger. Sunglasses matter more than you would think up there, take the spare pair. The flight from Kathmandu was delayed by a few hours, which ate into the first day. A very good few days.

title: Pokhara Helicopter Sightseeing Tour
author: Bea Hartley
heading: Five stars from us
text: Had a spare morning before our flight home, so we squeezed in the Pokhara Helicopter Sightseeing Tour. Brilliant decision. There was enough time at the landing site for photos and a hot drink. The pilot gave a running commentary on the peaks without talking over the whole flight. Oxygen was on board and the crew showed us how to use it. If you are on the fence, just book it.

title: Pokhara Helicopter Sightseeing Tour
author: Noah Murphy
heading: Long days, big views
text: I am a nervous flyer and nearly cancelled the Pokhara Helicopter Sightseeing Tour. Glad I did not. At one point I was above the clouds with nothing but summits showing. One of those trips that stays with you.

title: Pokhara Helicopter Sightseeing Tour
author: Astrid Long
heading: One for the memory bank
text: I took the Pokhara Helicopter Sightseeing Tour alone after a trek was cancelled, and it saved the trip. The noise-cancelling headsets were a small but welcome touch. Transfers were included and the car was comfortable. The window seats rotate so everyone gets a turn if you ask. Two weeks on and I am still looking at the photos.

title: Pokhara Helicopter Sightseeing Tour
author: Alexandra Ward
heading: Happy customers
text: Booked the Pokhara Helicopter Sightseeing Tour for a work team morning out, which was a better idea than it sounds. Would go back with the same team in a heartbeat.

title: Pokhara Helicopter Sightseeing Tour
author: Maja Kowalski

text: We had one free morning at the end of a work trip and spent it on the Pokhara Helicopter Sightseeing Tour. The view of Everest from the cockpit was better than anything we've seen from a trail. The team kept the group small, so boarding was quick and calm. Breakfast at the landing site was simple but welcome at that altitude. Good value for what you get.

title: Pokhara Helicopter Sightseeing Tour
author: Sofia Andersen

text: We had looked at the price three times before booking the Pokhara Helicopter Sightseeing Tour, and I am glad we did. title: Pokhara Helicopter Sightseeing Tour

The hour on the ground was long enough for a proper look around. Hotel pickup was on time, which after a week in Nepal felt like a small miracle. The group was a bit large on the first day, though it thinned out after the first village.

title: Pokhara Helicopter Sightseeing Tour
author: Bea Okafor
heading: Big views, good company
text: Two of us flew in the morning and went straight back to the hotel for a nap. Both sides of the aircraft get a good run at the mountains, so seating hardly matters. Ground staff picked us up on time and everything ran like clockwork. Would do it again without hesitating.

title: Pokhara Helicopter Sightseeing Tour
author: Ethan Jenkins
heading: A real highlight
text: My daughter and I did the Pokhara Helicopter Sightseeing Tour together and neither of us stopped grinning. Takeoff felt oddly relaxed, more like a scenic drive than an adventure sport.

title: Pokhara Helicopter Sightseeing Tour
author: Freja Okafor

text: The Pokhara Helicopter Sightseeing Tour was a birthday present from my wife and I could not have asked for better. About fifteen minutes in, the whole Himalaya opened up in front of us. Photos from the flight are on my wall now. Happy to recommend these guys to anyone heading to Nepal.

title: Pokhara Helicopter Sightseeing Tour

title: Pokhara Helicopter Sightseeing Tour
author: Olivia Brooks

title: Rafting in Bhote Koshi River
author: Sean Alvarez

text: We added Rafting in Bhote Koshi River to the end of a trek in September and it was the perfect change of pace. The jungle walk was slower than the jeep drives but we saw more smaller things. title: Rafting in Bhote Koshi River

text: Chose Rafting in Bhote Koshi River because it fit the days we had left. It delivered far more than expected. The jungle is thick, so sightings need patience, but the guides know where to look. author: Grace Ortiz

Lhakpa knew the difference between a fresh pug mark and an old one, which was half the fun. The jeep was open-sided, which was great for photos but dusty. One teahouse room was cramped for two people, but we were too tired to care. Worth the money and the early starts.

title: Rafting in Bhote Koshi River

Happy to recommend these guys to anyone heading to Nepal.

title: Rafting in Bhote Koshi River
